note: Corpus Corporum's transcription only — Migne's plate is not touched. Verified against the plate: archive.org patrologiaecurs04migngoog (on disk raw/scans/pl113/), PDF page = (column + 11) / 2, calibrated this session against the printed corner numbers (p. 287 = cols 563/564). Every site read at 450 dpi on a crop taken wider than its target word; the whole line read at each, per the 2026-08-23 rule that the neighbours are where the invisible class lives — and that rule paid twice here (see 0705C, and the note patch below, which was found while answering a different question).
class: Seven digitization corruptions and ONE NORMALIZATION. The corruptions divide into three sub-classes already on the register — plain letter substitution (qum/cum, camdem/eamdem, gloriostor/gloriosior, septilormem/septiformem), the UNJOINED LINE BREAK where the digitization dropped Migne's hyphen and left the halves apart (Judaeo rum, cuncto rum), and a FOURTH now added: a FUSION ACROSS A LINE BREAK WHERE MIGNE HAD NO HYPHEN AT ALL (integra mente -> integramente), the exact inverse of the unjoined break and distinct from 8946's rejoin, which doubled a syllable in front of a real hyphen.

patches.why: ⭐⭐ THE NORMALIZATION CLASS REACHES FIVE, and this is the first instance found in a NOTE rather than in the body, and the first where the tidying changes the LANGUAGE of the word. The plate prints '(Vide tome VIII operum.)' — 'tome', the FRENCH word, in an editorial note by a French editor pointing his reader to volume VIII of Jerome's works. Corpus Corporum silently turned it into the Latin ablative 'tomo', which construes perfectly and so is invisible to every downstream check. Read at 450 dpi and unambiguous. ⚑ Found while answering a different question entirely — whether Migne prints the text of Jerome's prologue at all (he does not: head, this note, rule, CAPUT PRIMUM, and the exposition begins). The internal spacing of the note is left exactly as Corpus Corporum sets it; only the word is corrected, because spacing is transcription convention and not a plate defect.

patches.find:
dicit eum qui integramente
Domino aedificare
patches.replace:
dicit eum qui integra
mente Domino aedificare
patches.why: the plate prints 'qui integra' at the end of one line and 'mente Domino aedificare' at the head of the next, WITH NO HYPHEN, because 'integra' is a whole word. The digitization joined the two words across the break and manufactured 'integramente', which is no Latin word. New sub-class: the hyphenless cross-line fusion.

the plate breaks the word as 'Judæo-' / 'rum' with the hyphen printed. The digitization dropped the hyphen and left the halves standing apart. Same class as 8992's 'Qui dam' and 8958's 'per verse'. ⚠ The word is CLOSED UP rather than the hyphen restored: our chunks reflow the TEI's line breaks into running text, so a restored hyphen would sit mid-line and be a new defect of our own. 8946 was closed up for the same reason.
the plate prints 'cum corpora eorum cum quibus in hac vita remanserunt'. 'qum' is no Latin word; the plate settles it as an ordinary q/c substitution.

the plate prints 'septiformem' — the sevenfold grace of the Spirit, which is what the sentence is about. ⚠ Worth recording: at 150 dpi the neighbouring word looked like 'Prophetia' and a second divergence seemed to be there; the 450 dpi crop shows 'Propheta', agreeing with our file exactly. A false suspicion killed by cropping properly, which is the same discipline that catches the true ones.

the plate prints 'gloriosior eris in regno Dei'. ⚠ The sentence stands BEFORE the [0709A] anchor, so it is physically the foot of col. 708 and was read at the bottom of the right column of PDF p. 359, not on p. 360. A column anchor marks where a column BEGINS; text above it belongs to the column before.
the plate prints 'unam et eamdem Ecclesiae figuram'. 'camdem' is no Latin word; e/c substitution.

the plate breaks the word as 'cuncto-' / 'rum' with the hyphen printed; the digitization dropped it. Same unjoined-break class as 0702A, and the two sit nine columns apart in one book. Closed up, not hyphenated, for the reason given there.

refuted.verdict: MIGNE'S — our file agrees with the plate. Raised only as an artefact of a 150 dpi impression and killed by the 450 dpi crop. Recorded because a checked negative is worth having.

MIGNE'S — our file agrees with the plate, and the suspicion is withdrawn. Unreadable in the archive.org copy (p. 354 clips the left margin) and settled 2026-08-24 against a SECOND WITNESS: Gallica bpt6k5505319w f349, full margin, which opens col. 697 with 'magistorum quasi ferramentis fabrorum praepa-rata'. ⚑ Worth keeping as a checked negative: the word was raised on a list of non-words and is in fact an ordinary genitive plural, so it never belonged to that class at all -- the class whose plate reads have been 19 for 19 stayed unbeaten.
